runs.title: Neighbour: falling knife measured with the Wilder ATR (TradingView ta.atr)
runs.question: Should the bot trade smaller when the setup fades a strong one-way move, i.e. price is stretched far from the 1-hour EMA 20 on the wrong side (a 'falling knife')?
runs.verdict: Better than the live strategy in both periods. 2026: net +$20,139 (live +$20,111), PF 3.49 (3.48), max DD -$2,660 (-$2,661), 2.16 trades/week. 2021-25: net +$9,639 (+$6,491), PF 1.13 (1.09), max DD -$9,944 (-$11,401), 3.17/week. Rule hit 51 setups in 2021-25 and 3 in 2026. Same EMA 20 and 3-ATR line, but the ATR is TradingView's / the engine's Wilder ATR, which is a bit wider, so it hits fewer setups (51 in 2021-25, 3 in 2026). This is the version the engine and the Pine script would naturally use. Honest caveat: it was a robustness check, noticed as the natural implementation only after 2026 had been seen; in 2026 it is simply unchanged (+$28).

sizing.rule: Neighbour: falling knife measured with the Wilder ATR (TradingView ta.atr)

runs.title: Trending-day breakeven at +3R + the sizing researcher's recommendation
runs.question: Do the two recommendations add up: breakeven at +3R on trending days plus quarter size in cold streaks and half size on late entries?
runs.verdict: Recommended pair. Against the sizing recommendation alone: 2026 the same (net +$20.5k vs +$20.6k, PF 3.94 vs 4.12, same eval passes, no eval fail within 3 months either way), 2021-25 another +$4.8k (PF 1.19 -> 1.27, 3-month eval passes 29.3% -> 32.8%). Against today's live rules it is better in both periods.
